reason: H0 directly fuzzes the UTF-8 validation surface implicated by the PPC64 `is_ascii` boundary correction. It passes arbitrary byte sequences and lengths to `validate_utf8` for every runtime-supported implementation and compares their results, so inputs containing the corrected boundary byte `0x80` can expose PPC64 disagreement. The `simd8x64` change only corrects a static-assert message and adds no runtime behavior requiring separate coverage.
evidence: S1 changes `is_ascii(const simd8x64<uint8_t>& input)` from subtracting `0b10000000u` to `0b01111111u`, explicitly noting that `0x80` is not ASCII.
H0 invokes `impl->validate_utf8((const char*)Data, Size)` with unrestricted fuzzer-controlled bytes and size.
H0 obtains `get_runtime_supported_implementations()` and compares `validate_utf8` results across those implementations, covering the PPC64 backend when it is runtime-supported.
The only other S1 change replaces the text `Westmere kernel` with `PPC64 kernel` inside a `static_assert` message without changing the assertion or executable semantics.
recommended_action: Keep H0 as the relevant harness; ensure it is built and run on PPC64-capable infrastructure so the PPC64 implementation is included in the runtime-supported set.
